# Survival Analysis and Time-to-Event Graphics

Time-to-event outcomes require specialized visual conventions. `cliplot()` implements Kaplan-Meier survival curves with aligned risk tables and Fine-Gray cumulative incidence curves for competing risks.

## Kaplan-Meier Curves: `type = "km"`

`cliplot(Surv(time, event) ~ arm, data, type = "km")` estimates the step survival function $\hat{S}(t)$:

$$\hat{S}(t) = \prod_{t_i \le t} \left(1 - \frac{d_i}{n_i}\right)$$

where $d_i$ is the number of events and $n_i$ is the number of individuals at risk at time $t_i$.

### Overall Survival with Landmark Milestones (NEJM Style)

Reporting overall survival (OS) requires both the step survival function and explicit landmark milestone rates (e.g., 6-month, 1-year, and 2-year survival) with confidence intervals.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(cliomicplot)
library(survival)
library(ggplot2)

clitheme("nejm")

p_km <- cliplot(
  Surv(time, status) ~ sex,
  data = lung,
  type = type_km(
    risk_table  = TRUE,
    pval        = TRUE,
    conf_int    = TRUE,
    median_line = TRUE,
    milestones  = c(180, 365, 730)
  ),
  palette  = "nejm",
  title    = "Overall Survival Stratified by Sex",
  subtitle = "NCCTG Lung Cancer Trial (n = 228) with 6-mo, 1-yr, 2-yr Milestones",
  xlab     = "Time on Study (days)",
  ylab     = "Survival Probability",
  legend   = "top"
)
p_km
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](03-survival-analysis_files/figure-html/km-demo-1.png){width=2400}
:::
:::


Key features of `type_km()`:
- Landmark milestones annotated directly on curves with percentage estimates and error bars.
- Aligned numbers-at-risk table matching x-axis tick positions.
- Dashed drop lines indicating median survival time for each cohort.

## Competing Risks Cumulative Incidence: `type = "ci"`

When evaluating disease progression, toxicities, or adverse event rates, clinical journals prefer cumulative incidence curves starting at 0% and climbing toward 100%:

$$F_k(t) = P(T \le t, C = k) = \int_0^t S(u-) d\Lambda_k(u)$$


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
clitheme("lancet")

p_ci <- cliplot(
  Surv(time, status) ~ sex,
  data = lung,
  type = type_km(
    cumulative_incidence = TRUE,
    risk_table           = TRUE,
    pval                 = TRUE,
    conf_int             = TRUE,
    milestones           = c(180, 365)
  ),
  palette  = "lancet",
  title    = "Cumulative Incidence of Mortality",
  subtitle = "NCCTG Lung Cohort — Landmark Milestones at 180 and 365 Days",
  xlab     = "Days Since Enrollment",
  ylab     = "Cumulative Incidence (%)",
  legend   = "top"
)
p_ci
```
